title: Geometry Worksheets: Lines, Rays, and Line Segments
intro: Use endpoints and arrows to distinguish lines, rays, and segments.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Draw all three and describe which directions continue. Explain that the picture represents an object that may extend beyond the paper.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Line: two arrows.
Ray: one endpoint and one arrow.
Segment: two endpoints.

The arrows mean the figure continues. They do not mean that the line stops at the arrow tip. Label each of your three drawings with its name.

Ask your student

Which drawing has exactly one endpoint?

If your student needs help

If the student judges only by drawn length, cover part of the line and discuss what its arrows mean.

Choosing and using the worksheet

This sheet reuses three fixed tasks: a parallel example, a perpendicular example, and a drawing task. Both example answers are Yes. New numbers does not supply different examples or negative cases.
